themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: TSMC's Q3 revenue was $46.72 billion (up 41.2%) with a 66.4% gross margin inside its 65% to 67% guide; it guided Q4 to $52.3 to $54.3 billion, raised 2026 growth to about 44% and kept 2026 capex at $60 to $64 billion, saying AI demand is far above supply. The stocks fell anyway as the selloff turned to debt: CoreWeave dropped about 15% on Oct 14 with its bonds near 15% yields, Oracle's five year CDS hit a record 288 basis points, Micron closed down 4.1% at $914.13, and on Oct 15 SK hynix fell about 11%, Samsung about 9.5% and Advantest about 15%.
themes.for_you: The chokepoint is fine; the borrowers are not. No chip or memory swings while the trend is down. NVDA is left out of both lists: TSMC's demand comments help it, but it fell 3.16% on Oct 14 with the group. ANET turned Buy zone now on Oct 13 data, before this selloff, so wait for the next refresh.

themes.name: Fintech and Crypto Rails: Stablecoins, Tokenization, Exchanges
themes.what: Schwab earned $1.69 a share adjusted (vs $1.66 expected) on about $7.17 billion of revenue, slightly light, with core net new assets up 38% to $190.4 billion and margin loans up 14% in the quarter to $187.9 billion (Oct 15). Bank of America closed Oct 14 down 4.76% at $51.39 after its miss and penalty.
themes.for_you: SCHW is Buy zone, wait for the chart: up/down volume is under 1.0 and needs to turn. Record margin borrowing is a warning for the market if the tech selloff deepens. No put on banks today.

themes.name: Healthcare and Medtech: Aging, Heart, Sugar, Hearing, Sight
themes.what: Health care was the best S&P 500 sector on Oct 14, up 2.44% while the index fell 1.11%, as money left tech after the hot CPI. UnitedHealth rose about 4.6% to 4.8%, a day after giving back its post earnings gap, and big drug makers rose about 3% to 4% midday (Merck 4.09%, AbbVie 3.94%, Lilly 3.38%). Abbott reports Q3 on Oct 21.
themes.for_you: This is a money flow move, not new clinical data, so it can reverse. LLY, PFE, GILD and MDT are Buy zone now on Oct 13 data; tranches fit. MDT and ABT are left out of both lists because their own moves were not reported; Abbott's Oct 21 report is the next test.

innovations.name: Space
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. Starship Flight 14 (Sep 28) was the first to reach orbit and deployed all 26 Starlink V3 satellites, though a vacuum engine failed and the stay in orbit was cut short; Flight 15 is penciled for no earlier than Oct 19 but not confirmed. SpaceX was reported Oct 6 to 7 to be seeking about $40 billion of debt to buy Nvidia chips. Planet Labs stock is down about 66% from its May peak even with record revenue, as money rotates to SpaceX and rates rise.
innovations.for_you: No action; none of these are on the swing or put lists. Reaching orbit keeps reusable launch at early adoption, not higher: no catch or refueling yet. RKLB is left out of both lists because nothing changed for Neutron. SPCX taking on $40 billion of debt fits today's worry about debt funded AI, so watch its bond pricing.

countries.name: European Union
countries.what: Zelenskyy told the Financial Times that Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian refineries because Russia kept hitting Ukraine's grid during the three day energy truce; on Oct 15 Russia said a drone set the Ryazan refinery on fire. The US is separately weighing easing shadow fleet tanker sanctions to cut freight costs.
countries.for_you: No action. A failed truce keeps diesel and European energy costs high, which helps TTE and keeps the ECB hiking. STLA is left out of both lists because the effect on carmakers is indirect.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: A Houthi spokesman said Oct 14 that attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports will continue 'in the coming days' (House of Saud citing Reuters and gCaptain; less established source). Reuters reported the US is weighing letting sanctioned tankers carry non sanctioned oil out of the Gulf to cut record freight rates; analysts expect only a few extra ships. Brent fell about 1.5% to about $104.44 on Oct 15.
countries.for_you: COP closed over its 141.91 pivot on Oct 14, but the volume is not confirmed yet; wait for Setups. FRO is left out of both lists: more tankers allowed would ease freight rates, but the threats to shipping keep them high.

countries.name: Japan
countries.what: The Nikkei fell 4.9% to 64,425.95 on Oct 15, its third biggest point drop ever, as the AI selloff spread from Korea and the US. Advantest fell about 15% and SoftBank Group 8% to 10%; Tokyo Electron fell about 5% to 8%. The yen firmed to just under 158 per dollar.
countries.for_you: No action. Advantest (6857.T) is the chip tester for AI chips and does not trade on a US exchange. SONY moves to mixed because a firmer yen trims exporters while its chip unit is in the selloff. TM and MUFG are left out of both lists because the move was in tech.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: The KOSPI plunged 7.57% to 5,554.22 on Oct 15 ('Black Thursday'), its seventh straight loss, with a sell side sidecar at 9:07am and a Level 1 circuit breaker at 12:38pm. SK hynix fell about 11% to 1,262,000 won and Samsung about 9.5% to 210,000 won. Analysts cited AI return doubts, China's CXMT and US rate hike risk.
countries.for_you: No action. Do not sell puts on EWY or MU into this; rich premiums reflect real risk. Korean banks stay hurt into the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision. CPNG is left out because its business is retail, not chips.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.what: TSMC beat and raised (Q3 revenue $46.72 billion, gross margin 66.4%, 2026 growth now about 44%, capex unchanged at $60 to $64 billion), yet its shares fell about 2% and the Taiex had its sixth steepest point drop with a record NT$302.56 billion of net foreign selling on Oct 15.
countries.for_you: No chip swings yet. TSM's business is fine, so it stays bullish on fundamentals, but it has no buy zone verdict. EWT is hurt by foreign selling. NVDA and AMD are left out: TSMC's demand comments help them, but they fell with the group premarket.
